reason: E2 mentions substrate heating as a strategy to mitigate hot cracking in HEAs, supporting the general premise, but none of the cited evidence provides specific data on temperature optimization (~300°C), quantified reductions in defects or stress, or direct links to dimensional precision and mechanical property improvements. E3 and E4 discuss process parameter effects and defects broadly but do not address substrate pre-heating. E1 is unrelated to pre-heating. Thus, the key premises are only loosely supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Substrate pre-heating reduces thermal gradients during L-PBF of HEAs
Reduced thermal gradients lower residual stress accumulation
Lower residual stress decreases defect density (pores, hot cracks) and dimensional inaccuracies
Reduced defects and residual stress enhance mechanical integrity
An optimized pre-heating temperature around 300°C is effective for HEA systems
